title: Linked Editing
content: ### ### ### Objective Copy and paste/mirror paste Patterns with Linked Editing function to edit them simultaneously. Or apply linked editing function to existing pair of symmetric Patterns (ver3.0.0). ### Location #### Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Clone Pattern with Linked Editing ▶ Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern #### Apply Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Apply Linked Editing ▶ Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern #### Remove Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Remove Linked Editing ### Operation #### Clone Pattern with Linked Editing 1. Select the Pattern to be duplicated with the Transform Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Clone Pattern with Linked Editing ▶ Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern 3. The clone of the Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. → Symmetric Patterns's outline is highlighted in light-blue (ver2.5.0). 4. Click on the 2D window to place the clone. → The selected Pattern is pasted/mirror pasted with Linked Editing function. ※ Note: When copying the Pattern as an instance (Instance Pattern,) right click on the 2D window to access the Paste window which allows you to set Interval and Number of Shapes. #### Apply Linked Editing 1. Select the patterns to be linked with the Transform Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Apply Linked Editing ▶ Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern → Selected Patterns are linked and can be edited simultaneously. #### Remove Linked Editing 1. Select the Patterns which the Linked Editing function should be removed with the Transform Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Remove Linked Editing → The applied Linked Editing function is removed.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on how to utilize the Linked Editing function for cloning, applying, and removing linked editing on symmetric patterns in design software.

title: Show 3D Garment Window Size
content: ### Objective Check 3D Garment window size in pixel. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show 3D Garment Window Size (F9) ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show 3D Garment Window Size (F9) → The result value of 3D Garment Window Size appears in pixel at the right-hand side and the bottom of the window. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline again to turn it off: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show 3D Garment Window Size (F9)
content_description: This web page provides instructions on how to check and toggle the 3D Garment window size in pixels within the application.

title: Copy Fabric
content: ### Objective Copy and modify an existing Fabric in order to change Fabric properties partially. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Copy ### Operation 1. Object Browser ▶ Select a fabric style to copy in the Fabric tab. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Copy → A new Fabric item with the same properties of the selected Fabric item is now being created.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for copying and modifying an existing Fabric to adjust its properties in the Object Browser.

title: Avatar (*.avt) Open/Save
content: ### Objective Save and load all Avatar related files, such as the Model (*.dae or *obj), Pose (*.pos), Motion (*.mtn), Accessories (*.acc), Bounding Volume (*.pan), and Arrangement Points (*.arr) as one file (*.avt). ### Location #### Open AVT Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar (Ctrl+Shift+A) #### Save AVT Main menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Avatar ### Operation #### Open AVT 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar (Ctrl+Shift+A) → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click Open to load it. ※ Note: The default avatars provided by Marvelous Designer are located in the following path. Windows Library ▶ Documents ▶ Marvelous Designer ▶ Assets_ver_x.x.x ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar (Detail Path) C: ▶ Users ▶ User Name ▶ Documents ▶ Marvelous Designer ▶ Assets_ver_x.x.x ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar #### Save AVT 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Avatar → The Open File window appears. 2. Select a location to save the Garment file, enter in a name and press Save button. ※ Note: Even if multiple Avatars exist within the workspace, they can be saved separately (ver2.3.0).
content_description: This web page provides instructions for saving and loading Avatar-related files in Marvelous Designer, allowing users to manage their Avatar assets efficiently.

title: 3D File (LXO) Export
content: ### Objective Export garments and avatars as LXO file format which is compatible with Modo. The LXO file format includes Geometry and Material information. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ LXO ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ LXO → The Save File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and the file name. Then, select Save. → The file is exported as a LXO file format.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for exporting garments and avatars as LXO files compatible with Modo, including geometry and material information.

title: Scene and Props Properties (ver.2024.0)
content: Set the Scene and Props properties. When you select a Scene and Props, its properties appear in the property window. **Scene and Props Properties** Properties | Description ---|--- Information | Model | You can change the type of Scene & Props Specification | Collision (ver. 2024.0) | Enable or disable collision handling. When collision is enabled, objects and clothing will collide. Collision Thickness | The thickness of the collision treatment on the surface of the object. Can be entered from 0 to 100. Material (Selected) | Set the [Material](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425) of the object. Miscellaneous | Mesh Type | Indicates the type of object mesh. Element Count | Indicates the number of points in the mesh.
content_description: This web page provides essential information and settings for configuring Scene and Props properties, including collision handling and material selection.

title: Set Language (Above ver 7.1.1)
content: ## Objective Marvelous Designer currently supports Korean, Chinese, English, Japanese, French, Portuguese, Taiwanese, Italiano, and Spanish. Set the language according to user preference. ## Location Main Menu ▶ Help ▶ Language ## Operation 1. Find and click the menu as below: Main Menu ▶ Help ▶ Language 2. Select the desired language. ※ Note: The program must be restarted for the change to take effect.
content_description: Easily change the language settings in Marvelous Designer to match your preferences by following simple steps in the Help menu.

title: Allowing remote access for Network offline license
content: Access ACC page ([http://localhost:1947)](http://localhost:1947) 1. Allow TCP 1947 port in the network section between the client PC and the license server (firewall, network equipment, etc.) 2. Allow external clients to use licenses on the license server ![1.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438681330969) 3. Setting the address of the license server on the client PC In order to allow clients on other networks to find the license server, please change settings as follow ![2.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438681438105) Enable Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses option Enter the address of the license server accessible to the Remote License Search Parameters *Please click the Submit button at the bottom to save changes.
content_description: This web page provides essential instructions for configuring network settings to enable external clients to access licenses from the license server.

title: Particle Distance Setting
content: ### Objective Particle Distance refers to the average distance between the points that make up a Garment Pattern, in other words, size of the mesh. The Garment quality and Simulation speed depend on the Particle Distance. Therefore set the value at 20mm when making a Garment and dressing it on an Avatar for faster working process, and set it under 5mm to enhance the Garment quality once it is completed. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Particle Distance ### Operation 1. Select Pattern(s). 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Particle Distance 3. Input desired value for the Particle Distance. (Minimum '0.8' to maximum '700.0') 4. Press Enter on keyboard to apply.
content_description: Optimize your garment simulation by adjusting the Particle Distance in the Property Editor to balance quality and speed effectively.

title: 3D 1:N Free Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Free Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Free Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Establish the start and the end point on the Pattern outline, which is called as 1, where multiple Patterns are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Line appears in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key, establish Sewing Lines on N Patterns. Similar to setting regular Free Sewing Lines, be careful with Directional Notches. 5. Release the Shift key to complete. ※ Note * While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide for users to establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes in both 2D and 3D environments, facilitating the seamless sewing of multiple patterns together.

title: Requesting Network Offline License Activation For A Separate License - Second or Above Installation (Window OS)
content: **Step 1.** Open[ ACC Page](http://localhost:1947) to make sure your server has the HASP Driver installed. If the following screen appears, then the installation is still functioning. ![unnamed.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438540241945) If not, install the HASP Driver by following the steps below. a. Download the driver from the link here. * Mac: <https://cdn.clo3d.com/HASP/Sentinel_Runtime_94691.tar> * Linux: <https://cdn.clo3d.com/HASP/aksusbd-8.31.1.tar> * Windows: <https://cdn.clo3d.com/HASP/haspdinst_8_31.exe> b. Press 'Windows Start Button + Run (R)' and then enter "CMD" in the text field to open the Command Prompt window. (Example) ![first_time_installation_EN_.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438540472089) c. Drag the downloaded haspdinst.exe file and drop it on the CMD window to automatically register the corresponding path, as shown underlined in the image below. Enter "-i" behind the automatically entered path and press 'Enter' on the keyboard to install. (Example) ![unnamed__1_.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438540642969) d. In a web browser, navigate to <http://localhost:1947> and check to see if the following screen appears to verify the HASP Driver has been successfully installed. ![unnamed.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438585686297) * If an error message pops up, please refer to the troubleshooting manual for “Sentinel HASP Driver Errors on Windows part”. ([Link to the Manual](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585)) **Step 2.** Now you're ready to create a new C2V file. Please download the Multi C2V Generator program and open it. (**C2V generator** [download](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e-VjEvJR-YdlaXhLLHJnta_nN4fNPgDe/view?usp=sharing)) **Step 3.** Click the folder icon, then you can set up the file name and designate the file path in the window that appears. ![step_3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438540930457) **Step 4.** Set up the file name with your preference, and click the ‘Save’ button. ![step_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438541173913) **Step 5.** Click the ‘Generate’ button in order to generate the file. ![step_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438541381273) **Step 6.** Check the file at designated location to make sure it has been created successfully. ![step_6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438541543833) Submit your C2V file to this [**page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (Login with company account is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com You will then receive a V2C file from our team to complete the application of the license to your server. ## **Applying a V2C on the server** In order to complete a license update with a V2C file, please follow the steps below. 1\. Download the V2C file sent to you from the Marvelous Designer Support Team. 2\. Click on the link below to access the ACC Page, then select “Update/Attach” in the Options section on the left. ([Click here to link ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)) ![v2c_application_1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438586544537) 3\. Click “Choose File” to find and select the downloaded V2C file. ![v2c_application_2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438586699033) 4\. Click “Apply File”. 5\. If the update is successful, the following message will be printed. ![v2c_application_3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438542272025) **[Double checking an updated License Key]** If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and navigate to the ACC Page 2\. Click ‘Features’ once you see the key info. ![v2c_application_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438542413849) 3\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed to the correct number of licenses. ![v2c_application_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438542550041)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for installing the HASP Driver, generating a C2V file, and applying a V2C file to update your license on the server for Marvelous Designer software.

title: Dart
content: ### Objective Create darts inside Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Dart 2D Toolbar ▶ Dart ### Operation #### Create Dart 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Dart 2D Toolbar ▶ Dart 2. Click and drag within the Pattern to create a Dart. 3. Release the mouse to complete the Dart. ### Create Dart with Dimension and Position 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Dart 2D Toolbar ▶ Dart 2. Click once within the Pattern. → The Create Dart window appears. 3. Enter the desired values for following options. Dimension | Enter the desired values for Width (Left,) Width (Right,) Height (Up,) Height (Down.) All values are measured from the center of the Dart. ---|--- Position | Outline | Designate the Dart's position within the Pattern by entering the margin between the Dart outline and the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). Center | Designate the Dart's position within the Pattern by entering the distance between the center of the Dart and the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: Internal Shape Tool Group
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the process of creating and customizing darts within 2D patterns using the provided tools and dimensions.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Rendering Thickness
content: ### Objective Set Fabric thickness for a Garment in the 3D Garment window. Rendering thickness from the center of the Garment is set for 0.5mm as the default value, and it is adjustable. This thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. ※ Note: To see the rendering thickness, the 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set on Thick Textured Surface. ### Location #### Fabric Unit Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶ Thickness #### Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0) Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Rendering ### Operation #### Fabric Unit 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶ Thickness 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied. #### Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Rendering 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting fabric thickness settings in the 3D Garment window, ensuring accurate rendering for garment design.

title: Attach Pin to/Detach Pin from Avatar
content: ### Objective Affix specific parts of the Garments to the Avatar. This function is commonly used for Simulation or recording animation for avoiding the Garment sliding off from the Avatar. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) ### Operation #### Attach Pin to Avatar 1. Create a pin to attach to an Avatar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) 3. Right-click on the created pin ▶ select Attach Pin to Avatar/Attach All Pins to Avatar. → The selected pin is now being attached to the nearest part of the Avatar. ※ Note: Pins attached to the Avatar are unable to be selected or moved. #### Detach Pin from Avatar 1. Right-click on the pin attached to the avatar ▶ select Detach from Avatar/Detach All Pins from Avatar. → The attached pin is now being detached from the Avatar.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for attaching and detaching garment pins to an Avatar for accurate simulation and animation recording.

title: Divide Internal Lines
content: ### Objective Cut and separate Internal Lines or points from an Internal Shape or continuous Internal Line. ### Location #### Divide Internal Point Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Point) ▶ Divide Internal Point #### Divide Internal Line Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Line) ▶ Divide Internal Line ### Operation #### Divide Internal Point 1. Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Point) ▶ Internal Point → The Internal Line is divided at the selected point. → The divided point is now indicated as a point with no fill. #### Divide Internal Line 1. Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Line) ▶ Divide Internal Line → The Internal Line is divided from its original Internal Shape. → Both ends of the Internal Line are indicated with points with no fill.
content_description: This webpage provides a concise guide on how to cut and separate internal lines or points from shapes using the Edit Pattern tool in a 2D design environment.

title: Save User Setting as Configuration File
content: ### Objective Save user settings such as language, measurement units, and shortcuts as a configuration file that can be applied to program updates. ### Location #### Save Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ User Setting #### Open Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ User Setting ### Operation #### Save 1. Configure the user settings as needed. 2. Locate the menu as below : Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ User Setting → The Save File window appears. 3. Assign the file name and location, then click Save. → The user settings is saved as a configuration file. #### Open 1. Locate the menu as below : Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ User Setting → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired configuration file and hit the Open button. → The information window appears, asking you to restart the program to apply the changes. 3. Restart the program. → The user settings contained within the configuration file is applied.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for saving and loading user settings as configuration files to ensure personalized preferences are retained across program updates.

title: Color Palette
content: Import existing color palettes from llustrator, Photoshop, or customize an own color palette and utilize it for design works (ver2.2.0).
content_description: "Effortlessly import and customize color palettes from Illustrator or Photoshop to enhance your design projects."

title: Select Mesh
content: ### Objective Click and drag to select Pattern Mesh freely. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select Mesh (Box) / Select Mesh (Lasso) 3D Toolbar ▶ (Click for more than 2 seconds) ▶ Select Mesh (Box) / Select Mesh (Lasso) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select Mesh (Box) / Select Mesh (Lasso) 3D Toolbar ▶ (Click for more than 2 seconds) ▶ Select Mesh (Box) / Select Mesh (Lasso) → The Garment Mesh is now displayed in green in both the 3D and 2D windows. → When using the tool, 3D tools, and Thick Textured Surface are disabled. 2. Click on a vertex (a point of the mesh). → The Mesh is now selected. 3. Or click on a desired area on the Garment ▶ Click and drag to select the area. → The selected area is displayed in green. → The selection also appears on the respective 2D Pattern. 4. Click and drag, or use the Gizmo to move the selected Mesh as desired in the 3D window. ※ Note: * Click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Shift+Ctrl on the keyboard to select additional mesh. Adversely, click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Ctrl on the keyboard to deselect Mesh from existing selected areas. * #### Select Segment Mesh Double-click on a Pattern outline in either the 3D or 2D window to select Mesh along the segment. When selecting Mesh on the Pattern in the 2D window, adjacent segment vertices are also selected when the angle difference is less than 20˚. * #### Select Mesh on the Pattern Double-click on a Pattern in either the 3D or 2D window to select all Mesh on a Pattern. * #### Select Mesh on Internal Line (v4.0.0) Use the same procedure as above to select mesh on specific Internal Lines and Shapes.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for users on how to efficiently select and manipulate garment mesh in a 3D environment using various selection tools.

title: Add Point to Pattern on Start/End
content: ### Objective Add point to Pattern outline on start or end point of a Sewing line. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing 2. Right click on the Sewing Line. → The right click pop-up menu appears. 3. At your need, add point to Pattern outline on either the start or the end point of the selected Sewing Line. → The point is added respective to the chosen option. ※Note: The point is added to the Pattern outline where the selected Sewing Line is placed on. The same procedure can be repeated to add a point to the pattern outline where the other half of the sewing line is placed
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to adding points to the Pattern outline at the start or end of a Sewing line within the editing tools.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Friction Coefficient
content: ### Objective Use this function to adjust the friction of Garments. The Friction Coefficient affects the friction between a Garment and another Garment. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Preset ▶ Friction Coefficient ![Friction.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438837070745)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the friction coefficient of garments to optimize their interaction with other fabrics in the Fabric Property Editor.

title: What is the product version support policy for Marvelous Designer?
content: ### Q. What is the product version support policy for Marvelous Designer? Product support is available for the versions listed below. ### The latest product version receives regular updates with new features and hotfixes, along with fast technical support. The level of technical support may vary depending on the product version. ### Please refer to the table below for more details. **Product version** | **Build version** | **Support Range** ---|---|--- Marvelous Designer 2025 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 2025.0 | Technical Support Software Updates and patches Marvelous Designer 2024 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 2024.0 | Technical Support Software Updates and patches Marvelous Designer 12 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 7.1 | Technical Support Software Updates and patches are NOT supported Marvelous Designer 11 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 7.0 | Technical Support Software Updates and patches are NOT supported * There are two methods for requesting technical support: "[Contact Us](https://marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact)" and "[Community Forum](https://connect.clo-set.com/community/qna)." The support scope includes issues encountered during program installation and execution. * Please note that it may be difficult to provide support for issues arising from the difference between the supported version OS at the time of purchase and the current OS in use during installation or execution. * If you hold an enterprise perpetual license, you can trade-in your perpetual license for a subscription license. For detailed information, please refer to [**enterprise trade-in policy**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/ko/support/news?postId=f16869c1b54c4ed697f2721cddfe1340). **NOT supported product version** | **Build version** | **support** ---|---|--- Marvelous Designer 10 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 6.0 | Not supported Marvelous Designer 9 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 5.1 | Not supported Marvelous Designer 8 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 4.2 | Not supported Marvelous Designer 7 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 3.2 | Not supported * Technical support and software updates and hotfixes have been discontinued, except for perpetual license holders, who will continue to receive limited assistance. * Limited assistance includes assistance with installer downloads and installations. * Versions below 7 cannot be downloaded via the website installer. If you have a perpetual license for a product version below 7, please[ contact our support team](https://marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact) for further assistance.
content_description: This webpage outlines the product version support policy for Marvelous Designer, detailing available technical support and software updates for different versions.

title: MODULAR MODE: Select a Block in the Modular Configurator Window
content: ### Objective Select and combine Blocks as desired in the Modular Configurator window. ### Location Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ Modular Configurator ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ Modular Configurator → Modular Configurator window appears. 2\. Select a desired category from the horizontal tab. → Folders appear in order. 3\. Select a desired Garment category folder. → Modular Structure file is displayed. 4\. title: Open Auto Save File (.Zpac or .Zprj)
content: ### Objective Open files that are auto-saved when the program closes unexpectedly due to a power failure or error. ※ Note: * From ver3.1.0, project file (*.zprj) will be auto saved. * File is auto saved every three minutes. Therefore, auto save files only contains work completed three minutes prior to power/ program failure. ### Location #### By Opening the Program Launch Marvelous Designer ▶ Auto Save File pop-up #### By Locating the File C: ▶ Users ▶ User Name ▶ Documents ▶ Marvelous Designer ▶ Assets_ver_x.x.x ▶ Autosave ### Operation #### By Opening the Program 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Launch Marvelous Designer ▶ Auto Save File pop-up → The auto-saved file opens. #### By Opening the Folder 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: C: ▶ Users ▶ User Name ▶ Documents ▶ Marvelous Designer ▶ Assets_ver_x.x.x ▶ Autosave 2. Double-click autosave.zpac/ autosave.zprj file created in the folder. → The program starts and the auto saved file opens. ※ Note: #### Auto Save File Location You can changed the folder in which Auto Save files are saved via (ver2.3.0): Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Default Files ▶ Auto Save ▶ Select file path
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to access auto-saved files in Marvelous Designer, ensuring users can recover their work after unexpected program closures.

title: MODULAR MODE: Module Structure
content: Module is a system that allows you to adjust the designs easily and combine them part by part. Please see the terminology for the Module below in order to have a better understanding in the Modular Mode. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438537801881) A: Module Structure: A state when a Block Box that consists of a Garment is sewn to another. When sewing a Block Box that is in this Block Structure to a Pattern, it automatically creates Sewing Lines in between the Patterns as it is already interlocked. B: Pattern: Patterns to be included in a Block that will be adjusted partially. Patterns in the Modular Mode can be modified and sewn the same as the Simulation Mode. C: Block Box: A frame that consists of a Module Structure. D: Block: A state when Patterns are sewn to Block Boxes. Blocks that have the same Block Boxes can be replaced with each other.
content_description: Explore the Modular Mode of our system to easily adjust and combine designs part by part, enhancing your creative workflow.

title: UV EDITOR MODE: Change Normal Map Blending Method
content: ### Objective This feature allows users to select the Normal Map Blending Method that provides the best results for their intended use. ### Location Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ Graphic Options ▶ Normal Map Blending ### Operation 1. Load garment with a blended normal map component, → Example: Topstitching with the Type changed to "Texture" and the check box next to "3D" activated in the Property Editor. 2. Change a window view mode to UV Editor, and change the display channel to Normal Map. 3. Open Settings/Preferences in the Main Menu at the top of the interface, then select 'Preferences'. → Move the Preferences window so that it does not cover the UV Editor. 4. In the Preferences window, under Graphics Options, change the 'Normal Blending Method'. → Observe the normal map for blended Normal Map components is changed. 5. Bake out the normal map using the 'Bake Textures' option at the top of the UV Editor for application to the garment in an external 3D environment.
content_description: This web page guides users on how to select and adjust the Normal Map Blending Method to optimize their 3D garment designs.

title: Requesting Network Software License activation - First Time installation (Mac OS)
content: **[Software License Key for Network Offline] Generate a C2V for First Time Installation - Mac OS** **1\. Install a Run-time Environment on Mac OS following by steps below (step1, step2)** **Step 1.** Unzip Sentinel_Runtime.tar ([Sentinel Runtime](https://s3.amazonaws.com/s3.md.web.upload/newmdweb/helpcenter/installer/Sentinel_Runtime.tar) **Download**) **Step 2.** Run SentinelRuntimeInstallerCLI (Command Line Interface) and install on Mac’s terminal Once you are completed with steps above(step1, step2), you’re ready to generate a C2V file for the first time installation of an SL key. **Step 3.** Open a web browser and navigate to **[ACC Page](http://localhost:1947)** **Step 4.** Click on the “Fingerprint” button to create a C2V file. ![pasted_image_0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438507392153) **Step 5.** Submit your C2V file to this [**page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (Login with company account is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com **Step 6.** Please refer below to complete a V2C key update. **[Applying a V2C on the server]** 1\. Download the V2C file sent from Marvelous Designer Support Team. 2\. Click on the link below to access the ACC Page, then select “Update/Attach” in Options on the left. **(Click here to link[ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html))** ![v2c_application_1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438479628185) 3\. Click “Choose File” to find and select the downloaded V2C file. ![v2c_application_2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438479878297) 4\. Click “Apply File”. 5\. If the update is successful, the following message will be printed. ![v2c_application_3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438507936921) **[Double checking an updated License Key]** If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and navigate to [**ACC Page**](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 2\. Click Features once you see the key info. ![v2c_application_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438480194073) 3\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed to the correct number. ![v2c_application_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438508320025)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for generating a C2V file and updating a software license key on Mac OS for offline network installations.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Buckling Stiffness
content: ### Objective Adjust how much percentage (%) of total Bending intensity to use to decide the Buckling Stiffness of the corners of Fabric. This is used alongside Bending-Weft/Warp. For instance, entering a Buckling Stiffness of 80 when Bending value is 60, is going to result in the Bending value of the actual intensity of the part of the Fabric being folded being 80% of 60 which is 48. In other words, the higher the Buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the corners of fabric, and on the other hand, the lower the the ratio, the easier it folds. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ Buckling Stiffness-Weft/Warp ![____.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438785993753)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the percentage of total Bending intensity to determine the Buckling Stiffness of fabric corners, facilitating optimal fabric folding behavior in design applications.
